events.extended_summary: Spain has ordered olive oil mills to store 12% of their production from November 2026 to regulate supply by temporarily taking some oil off the market.The measure, published on Friday in Spain’s Official State Gazette (BOE), applies to the output each mill reports producing each month. Mills can store the oil either at their own facilities or at a third-party site.The Directorate-General for Agricultural Production and Markets said the measure excludes output reported for October and earlier months. The oil put into storage must stay off the market until 30 September 2027, the end of the season.The decision comes as Spain expects a strong harvest and already has high stocks. According to the resolution, opening stocks stood at 357,040 tonnes, while production is forecast to reach 1,602,596 tonnes.The expected supply could push producer prices down further. events.micro_summary: Why Spain is taking 188,000 tonnes of olive oil off the market.

events.extended_summary: Russia and Ukraine launched overnight drone attacks against each other's industrial sites and energy infrastructure on Friday. In Russia's southern Krasnodar region, drone debris fell onto an industrial facility in Afipsky and sparked a fire at the Afipsky oil refinery, which has a processing capacity of 9.1 million metric tons of crude per year, around 3% of Russia's national total. The plant produces gasoline and Euro-5 diesel and has been repeatedly targeted since the 2022 invasion, with previous attacks in August and July. Russia's Defense Ministry said it intercepted 142 Ukrainian drones across Russia and annexed Crimea. Ukraine reported shooting down or jamming 196 Russian drones, with impacts recorded at 22 locations. The Russian attacks caused power outages across seven Ukrainian regions, including Kyiv and Kharkiv, with emergency crews partially shutting down the capital region's grid due to heavy damage.
events.micro_summary: Russia and Ukraine exchanged overnight drone attacks, with Russia intercepting 142 Ukrainian drones and Ukraine downing 196 Russian drones.
events.summary: Russia and Ukraine launched overnight drone attacks on each other's industrial and energy infrastructure Friday, with debris hitting an oil refinery in Krasnodar and power outages reported across seven Ukrainian regions including Kyiv.

events.extended_summary: Opportunity Party leader Qiulae Wong has been described as the kingmaker in New Zealand's election after her party gathered over 5% of the counted votes. Under New Zealand's "mixed member proportional" system, each voter casts a party vote and an electorate vote, making single-party governments uncommon. Election polls show no clear frontrunner, meaning major parties will likely negotiate coalitions or confidence-and-supply agreements with minor parties after the election. Prime Minister Christopher Luxon indicated the National Party would work with current coalition partners ACT and New Zealand First, while Labour, the Green Party and Te Pāti Māori could form a left-leaning bloc. The Opportunity Party has stated it is prepared to work with either side, though Luxon has ruled out working with them. With just over 20% of votes typically being special votes, close races may not be decided until final results are published on November 27.
events.micro_summary: Opportunity Party leader Qiulae Wong emerges as kingmaker with over 5% of votes in New Zealand election.
events.summary: Opportunity Party leader Qiulae Wong is positioned as kingmaker after gathering over 5% of counted votes in New Zealand's election, with no clear frontrunner and major parties preparing coalition negotiations under the MMP system.

events.extended_summary: Donald Trump appointed Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff on Friday, replacing Susie Wiles just days after Republicans suffered sweeping losses in Tuesday's midterm elections that ended their control of Congress. Miller, a longtime adviser and architect of the administration's aggressive immigration enforcement policies, posted on X that he was "honored beyond words" and vowed to "fight with all of our soul to support our president." Trump stated Miller "gets it" and has been with him since the beginning. The appointment drew sharp criticism from Democratic lawmakers, who called Miller a "hatemonger," "xenophobe," and "dangerous extremist," with some demanding he be fired. Republican allies celebrated the move, with White House communications director Steven Cheung calling Miller a "Trump OG" and the biggest advocate for the Trump agenda. Miller previously served as deputy chief of staff for policy and was known for controversial statements about immigration enforcement operations.
events.micro_summary: Trump named Stephen Miller White House chief of staff following Republican midterm defeat.
events.summary: Donald Trump appointed Stephen Miller as White House chief of staff, replacing Susie Wiles, days after Republicans lost congressional control in midterm elections. Democrats condemned the move while Republicans celebrated the appointment of the immigration policy architect.

events.extended_summary: In Tuesday's midterm elections, Democrats achieved a 16% swing in the popular vote for the House of Representatives, a margin exceeding the 11.2% swing recorded in the November 1974 Watergate midterms following Richard Nixon's resignation. The results swept Republicans from their deepest heartlands. Donald Trump will remain in the Oval Office for a further two years and 10 weeks. Trump had spent months attempting to undermine the elections through gerrymandering districts and preparing claims that the vote was rigged, but these efforts failed as the democratic system proved resilient. Beyond the United States, Trump allies also suffered defeats in Serbia and Brazil, while Viktor Orbán fell from power in April.
events.micro_summary: Democrats win 16% House popular vote swing in midterms, defeating Republicans.
events.summary: Democrats secured a 16% swing in the House popular vote in Tuesday's midterm elections, surpassing the 1974 Watergate midterm swing of 11.2% and sweeping Republicans from their strongholds while Trump remains president for two years and 10 weeks.

events.extended_summary: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña was impeached by Congress and placed under house arrest minutes later after the collapse of Ueno Bank left 2.9 million people, about 60% of the adult population, unable to access their savings. The Senate voted 44-45 to remove him, rejecting his resignation attempt and stripping him of presidential immunity. Peña faces investigation for illicit enrichment, money laundering, influence peddling, and conflicts of interest related to the bank, which was suspended amid irregularities. Vice-President Pedro Alliana was sworn in as interim president until 2028, promising compensation for affected depositors. Protests erupted across the country, with some clashes between demonstrators and police. Peña, who denied wrongdoing, was detained at his home after lawmakers from his own party voted for his removal.
events.micro_summary: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña was impeached and placed under house arrest after Ueno Bank's collapse froze 2.9 million accounts.
events.summary: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña was impeached by a 44-45 Senate vote and placed under house arrest minutes later after Ueno Bank's collapse left 2.9 million people without access to their savings, sparking nationwide protests.

events.extended_summary: Global average temperatures have risen approximately 1.5°C above 19th-century levels, with the first halves of 2024, 2025, and 2026 marking the hottest periods on record. The world remains on track for 2.7°C of heating, while greenhouse gas emissions continue rising. As of early August 2026, nearly 50,000 wildfires were burning globally, with over 34,000 out of control, killing approximately 1.5 million people annually. The UN has accepted that global warming will exceed 1.5°C, and scientists have concluded that the rate of warming has effectively doubled over the past decade. Researchers warn that the world may be approaching climate tipping points that could trigger cascading warming toward a "Hothouse Earth" scenario, potentially raising temperatures beyond any level seen in the past 1.2 million years. New research suggests that as climate change worsens, political action to stop it may become increasingly difficult, creating a disastrous acceleration toward further warming.
events.micro_summary: Climate crisis accelerates with 1.5°C warming and 50,000 global wildfires as tipping points loom.
events.summary: Global average temperatures have risen 1.5°C above 19th-century levels, with the first halves of 2024, 2025, and 2026 recording the hottest on record, while nearly 50,000 wildfires burn worldwide and scientists warn of approaching climate tipping points.

events.extended_summary: Usman Khawaja, who retired after Australia's 4-1 Ashes series win over England, has claimed in his book Sabr that the entire Australian dressing room knew about the 2018 Cape Town ball-tampering scandal, stating "It was all of us. Not the batters, not the bowlers, not the staff. All of us." This contradicts Cricket Australia's conclusion that only Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft had prior knowledge of the sandpaper plot, resulting in one-year suspensions for Smith and Warner and a nine-month ban for Bancroft. Khawaja alleges the team openly debated roughing up the ball earlier in the South Africa tour and that Bancroft volunteered to use sandpaper during the Gqeberha Test. He also notes staff involvement during the Newlands Test. Cricket Australia has defended its investigation, stating it remains "comfortable" with its findings. Former coach Darren Lehmann revealed Khawaja had not spoken to him before publishing the book.
events.micro_summary: Usman Khawaja claims entire Australian team knew of 2018 ball-tampering plot after 4-1 Ashes series win.
events.summary: Usman Khawaja claims in his book Sabr that the entire Australian dressing room knew about the 2018 Cape Town ball-tampering scandal, contradicting Cricket Australia's finding that only Steve Smith, David Warner and Cameron Bancroft were aware.

events.extended_summary: Kalyn Ponga returned from a broken arm suffered 23 days earlier to lead New Zealand to a 34-10 victory over Tonga in a tense, weather-affected Rugby League World Cup semifinal. Ponga contributed three try assists and a try-saving tackle. Other New Zealand scorers included Jahrome Hughes, who scored twice, Xavier Willison, and Charnze Nicoll-Klokstad, who grounded a final-play kick from Erin Clark. Jamayne Isaako converted four goals. The match was played in strong wind and rain, with Tonga struggling against the conditions. New Zealand will face either Australia or Samoa in the final next Sunday at Lang Park in Brisbane. Separately, New Zealand's women's team also advanced to their World Cup final after a 32-0 semifinal win over Fetu Samoa.
events.micro_summary: Kalyn Ponga led New Zealand to a 34-10 Rugby League World Cup semifinal victory over Tonga.

events.extended_summary: No. 1 Miami (8-0) will visit No. 11 Notre Dame (7-1) at Notre Dame Stadium in South Bend on November 7 at 7:30 PM ET in a Week 10 college football matchup with major College Football Playoff implications. The game is considered a 'win or go home' situation for the Fighting Irish, who lost to BYU on October 17 after winning 16 consecutive games by double digits. Notre Dame is favored by 5.5 points with an over/under of 57.5. Miami, which began the season 8-0 following a national title game loss to Indiana, will be without star wideout Malachi Toney due to an ankle injury. Notre Dame will be short-handed defensively, missing middle linebacker Drayk Bowen, cornerback DJ McKinney, and safety Brauntae Johnson.
events.micro_summary: No. 1 Miami (8-0) visits No. 11 Notre Dame (7-1) in Week 10 with playoff implications.

events.extended_summary: Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur met with drivers Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc at Interlagos ahead of the São Paulo Grand Prix to address their first-lap clash at the Mexico Grand Prix. During the race at the Autódromo Hermanos Rodríguez, Leclerc attempted to pass Hamilton at Turn Four, causing both cars to run wide. Leclerc received a penalty while Hamilton was passed by Max Verstappen, who won the race, denying Ferrari a likely victory and potential one-two. Vasseur condemned the incident as showing a lack of respect and confirmed talks took place Thursday evening, stating the team comes first. Hamilton has publicly criticized Leclerc and called for clearer rules of combat. Ferrari hopes to compete for the championship next season, but internal conflict risks undermining ambitions for a 2027 title tilt.
events.micro_summary: Fred Vasseur reminded Ferrari drivers Hamilton and Leclerc that the team comes first after their Mexico clash.
events.summary: Ferrari team principal Fred Vasseur held a meeting with Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc at Interlagos ahead of the São Paulo Grand Prix, reminding them the team comes first after their first-lap clash in Mexico allowed Max Verstappen to win.

events.extended_summary: A Kenyan court sentenced doomsday cult leader Paul Mackenzie to 200 years in prison for murdering 191 people, all but one of them children, in Shakahola forest. The court found Mackenzie bore primary criminal culpability for instructing followers to starve their children to death so they could meet Jesus. He received 100 years for homicide and 100 years for starvation-related offences, to run consecutively. Mackenzie was arrested in 2023 after more than 400 bodies were discovered in shallow graves. He was tried alongside 28 accomplices who received sentences of up to 160 years. Of the 191 victims, 183 died from starvation, including 182 children and one adult, while eight children were suffocated, strangled or beaten to death. The judge declined to impose the death penalty, stating it would fail to achieve deterrence and could strengthen the convicts' beliefs. Mackenzie preached that the world would end in August 2023 and that fasting would bring followers closer to God.
events.micro_summary: Paul Mackenzie sentenced to 200 years in prison for murdering 191 people, all but one children.
events.summary: A Kenyan court sentenced cult leader Paul Mackenzie to 200 years in prison for murdering 191 people, all but one of them children, by ordering starvation in Shakahola forest.

events.extended_summary: A Learjet 60 traveling from Austin, Texas, to the Bahamas crashed into a six-lane highway in Palm Beach County, Florida, on Sunday around 12:50 local time, killing all nine people onboard. The aircraft nosedived into Military Trail near Greenacres and exploded on impact, creating a large crater that partially filled with water from severe storms. Among the seven passengers killed were tech entrepreneur Adam Robinson, his wife Helen Sharp, their children Emma, four, and Charlie, two, and family friends Rachael Reed and Charm. The 20-year-old co-pilot, Nathalia Gadelha Filgueiras, also died. Investigators believe parts of the jet may have broken off while airborne, with debris scattered across sports fields, businesses, and homes. Air traffic control recordings captured the crew reporting moderate turbulence, icing, and precipitation before declaring an emergency as the plane descended at 10,000 to 20,000 feet per minute in an overspeed condition. Gadelha Filgueiras, who earned her pilot's license at 17, was praised by her family as a tough and professional aviator.
events.micro_summary: A Learjet 60 crashed in Florida killing all nine onboard, including a tech entrepreneur and his young family.
events.summary: A Learjet 60 bound for the Bahamas crashed into a Florida highway Sunday, killing all nine onboard amid severe storms. Investigators believe parts may have broken off mid-air.

events.extended_summary: Six-year-old Elliot English died on Friday at Children's Health Ireland hospital in Crumlin from injuries sustained in a fire on 13 October in the Birchwood area of Waterford city. His parents, Kim and Philip English, and his brothers Callum, 12, and Jayden, nine, were also killed in the blaze, bringing the total number of family members who died to five. Another child remains in critical condition in hospital. Police launched a multiple murder investigation into the suspected arson attack. Jessica Dalton, 31, and Cian Stacey, 21, appeared in court charged with one count of criminal damage and two counts of assault causing serious harm, and were remanded in custody until 17 November. A sixth person arrested in connection with the fire was released without charge.
events.micro_summary: Six-year-old Elliot English died Friday, bringing the death toll to five in the Waterford arson attack.
events.summary: Six-year-old Elliot English died Friday from injuries sustained in a 13 October house fire in Waterford that killed his parents and two brothers. Another child remains critically injured. Two people are charged in connection with the suspected arson attack.

events.extended_summary: A fresh wave of bomb threats disrupted air traffic across Europe on Friday, affecting at least 18 flights from Bulgaria, Cyprus, Czechia, France, Hungary, Italy, Portugal, Romania and the UK. All landed safely with no explosives found. The alerts followed threats on Tuesday and Thursday forcing 35 flights to divert. Hungary scrambled fighter jets three times to escort civilian flights, including nine from Prague, four over France, two to Sofia and one from Lisbon to Rome. Affected flights were 0.0674% of 26,709 scheduled Friday. Media outlets in Ireland and the UK including RTÉ, the Irish Independent, NewstalkFM, TodayFM and Sky were evacuated after threats. A group warned "This is only the beginning." No link was established between airline and media threats, though Ireland called it a likely coordinated campaign. Taoiseach Micheál Martin said the threats aimed to sow fear.
events.micro_summary: A coordinated wave of bomb threats disrupted at least 18 European flights and media outlets on Friday.
events.summary: Bomb threats disrupted at least 18 flights across Europe on Friday, with all aircraft landing safely and no explosives found, while media organizations in Ireland and the UK were also evacuated amid warnings of a coordinated campaign.

events.extended_summary: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings Ltd filed its draft red herring prospectus with the Securities and Exchange Board of India for a proposed initial public offering structured entirely as an offer for sale. Promoter Hindustan Coca-Cola Overseas Holdings Pte. Ltd. plans to sell up to 99.74 crore equity shares, with shares to be listed on the BSE and NSE. The issue is expected to be worth approximately $1 billion, targeting a valuation of around $10 billion. Since it is entirely an OFS, the company will not receive any proceeds. The Coca-Cola Company holds 60% of HCCH, while Jubilant Beverages owns the remaining 40%. For the three months ended June 30, 2026, HCCH reported revenue of ₹4,310.17 crore, up 20.46% year-on-year, with sales volumes increasing 18.61% and EBITDA margin improving to 17.20%. The company operates through 2,273 distributors covering 1.7 million retail outlets, with 14 production facilities.
events.micro_summary: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings filed IPO papers to sell 99.74 crore shares for a $10 billion valuation.
events.summary: Hindustan Coca-Cola Holdings filed its draft IPO prospectus with Sebi for an offer for sale of up to 99.74 crore shares by its promoter, targeting a $10 billion valuation while reporting 20.46% revenue growth.

events.extended_summary: Priyanka Chopra Jonas announced Ventilator 2, a sequel to the 2016 Marathi film Ventilator, marking a decade since her production debut with Purple Pebble Pictures. The film will be produced by Priyanka Chopra Jonas, Dr Madhu Chopra and Rajesh Mapuskar under Purple Pebble Pictures and Magij Pictures. Mapuskar, who wrote and directed the original, will return in the same roles. The sequel is expected to release in 2027, though cast and storyline details remain undisclosed. The original Ventilator, released in 2016, revolved around the Kamerkar family gathering at a hospital after elderly member Gajanan was placed on a ventilator before Ganesh Chaturthi. The film combined humour with serious moments and won three National Film Awards, including Best Director for Mapuskar, Best Editing and Best Sound Mixing. Priyanka Chopra Jonas made a special appearance in the original. The announcement coincided with Purple Pebble Pictures completing 10 years in the industry. The project represents a production commitment rather than an acting role for the actress.
events.micro_summary: Priyanka Chopra Jonas announced Ventilator 2, a sequel to her 2016 Marathi film, scheduled for 2027 release.
events.summary: Priyanka Chopra Jonas announced Ventilator 2, a sequel to her 2016 Marathi production Ventilator, produced by Purple Pebble Pictures and Magij Pictures with Rajesh Mapuskar returning as director, scheduled for release in 2027.

events.extended_summary: Suriya and Jithu Madhavan's film 'Scene' earned Rs 34.25 crore worldwide on its opening day, November 6, collecting Rs 19.15 crore net in India and Rs 22.25 crore domestic gross. The Tamil version contributed Rs 16.15 crore net from 4,878 shows at 57.1% occupancy, while the Telugu version added Rs 3 crore through 1,289 shows at 47.1% occupancy. Overall theatre occupancy reached 55% across 6,167 shows, with an estimated 14,31,494 tickets sold. The film surpassed Suriya's previous release 'Vishwanath and Sons', which had earned Rs 15.35 crore net in India and Rs 31.74 crore worldwide. 'Scene' secured a worldwide opening advantage of Rs 2.51 crore, though its overseas collection of Rs 12 crore was lower than the previous film's Rs 14 crore.
events.micro_summary: Suriya's 'Scene' earned Rs 34.25 crore worldwide on its opening day.
events.summary: Suriya and Jithu Madhavan's 'Scene' collected Rs 34.25 crore worldwide and Rs 19.15 crore net in India on its opening day, surpassing the opening of Suriya's previous film 'Vishwanath and Sons'.

events.extended_summary: Tamil actor Vijay Sethupathi is set to make history as the first Indian actor to present an award at the 54th International Emmy Awards, scheduled for November 23, 2026, in New York. The ceremony, presented by the International Academy of Television Arts & Sciences, recognizes excellence in television programming produced outside the United States. Producer Kavita Gupta, a board member of the Academy, facilitated Sethupathi's participation. The actor recently appeared in Baththa and will next star in Mani Ratnam's Inji Vellam alongside Sai Pallavi and Thiagarajan Kumararaja's Pocket Novel. Additionally, his 2024 action drama Maharaja is being developed for a Hollywood remake while a sequel is in development.
events.micro_summary: Vijay Sethupathi becomes first Indian actor to present at 54th International Emmy Awards on November 23, 2026.
events.summary: Tamil actor Vijay Sethupathi will present at the 54th International Emmy Awards in New York on November 23, 2026, becoming the first Indian actor to do so at the ceremony honoring international television.

events.extended_summary: New Delhi The global artificial intelligence (AI) investment cycle may have peaked or could be entering a mid-cycle correction, with rising financing costs and concerns over the returns on massive capital expenditure likely to weigh on technology investments in the coming year, according to a Jefferies report. Jefferies in its report said financial markets were increasingly signalling reluctance to fund AI-related investments, raising questions over the sustainability of spending by major US technology companies. “All of the above suggests the AI capex cycle may have peaked, or at least commenced a mid-cycle correction,” the report said. The report noted that the four major hyperscalers -- Microsoft, Amazon, Alphabet and Meta -- increased their combined capital expenditure by 108 per cent year-on-year to USD 202 billion in the third quarter of 2026. Read also: US midterms could accelerate stock market rotation; Goldman Sachs sees healthcare as ‘next leg of AI trade’

events.extended_summary: Mumbai/Bengaluru, Nov. 7 -- It's boom time for data centres in India and their chief executive officers. Financials reported by India's top data centres reviewed by Mint show that as they raked in higher revenue, their chiefs were handsomely rewarded. Manoj Paul, managing director of the Indian operations of Redwood City, California-based data-centre company Equinix, emerged as the top earner, taking home Rs.5.91 crore in annual pay, although this was down 13% from FY24. While Equinix did not disclose if Paul's salary was tweaked because of equity-linked payouts, it coincided with the company reporting its slowest annual revenue growth since Paul took charge in September 2021. Ashish Arora, CEO of Nxtra by Airtel, saw his remuneration rise largely in line with the company's annual growth in earnings. events.extended_summary: India captain Shubman Gill won a delayed toss and elected to bowl in the second one-day international against New Zealand in Wellington, a match reduced to 47 overs per side due to rain. India bowled out New Zealand for 134 runs in 41 overs, with Gurnoor Brar taking four wickets while Auqib Nabi and Axar Patel claimed two wickets each. Daryl Mitchell scored a half-century and Mitchell Santner made 31 runs for the hosts. India needs 135 runs to secure victory and holds a 1-0 series lead after winning the first rain-affected match in Auckland by five wickets, where Virat Kohli scored 74. Both teams were unchanged from the first match. Virat Kohli celebrated his 38th birthday in Wellington on Thursday. India previously won a five-match Twenty20 series 3-2.
events.micro_summary: India bowled out New Zealand for 134 in the rain-reduced second ODI in Wellington, needing 135 to win.

events.summary: India captain Shubman Gill chose to bowl after winning the toss in the rain-reduced second ODI in Wellington, with India bowling New Zealand out for 134 in 41 overs and needing 135 runs from 47 overs to win.

events.extended_summary: India secured a four-run victory over New Zealand via the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method in the rain-affected second ODI in Wellington, taking a commanding 2-0 lead in the five-match series. The match was reduced to 47 overs per side, with New Zealand bowled out for 134 in 41 overs after India's seam attack dismantled the hosts, dismissing openers Tim Seifert and Will Young through Auqib Nabi and captain Tom Latham and Glenn Phillips via Gurnoor Brar's double strike. Daryl Mitchell top-scored with 55. Chasing the revised target, India were 113-7 off 26 overs when rain ended play, four runs ahead of the DLS par score of 109. Jacob Duffy claimed 3-35, dismissing Shubman Gill for a golden duck and Virat Kohli for seven, while Kyle Jamieson took 3-35 including Shreyas Iyer for 30. KL Rahul remained unbeaten on 26. India require one more win to clinch the series.
events.micro_summary: India defeated New Zealand by four runs via DLS to take a 2-0 series lead in Wellington.
events.summary: India beat New Zealand by four runs via the Duckworth-Lewis-Stern method in a rain-reduced second ODI in Wellington, taking a 2-0 lead in the five-match series after the hosts were bowled out for 134.

events.extended_summary: Three workers died in an explosion and fire at Oil India Limited's Intermediate Tank Farm in Tengakhat, Assam's Dibrugarh district, during maintenance work on Friday. Nine workers were present when the accident occurred, with seven sustaining injuries. Raju Dutta died on Friday, while Tapas Jyoti Gogoi and Rupam Gohain succumbed to burn injuries on Saturday. Gogoi, who suffered approximately 70 percent burns, died around 3 am Saturday and had worked at the facility for 13 years. Three to four injured workers remain under advanced medical treatment, with one or two in critical condition. The injured were initially taken to Assam Medical College and Hospital before being shifted to a private healthcare facility. The exact cause of the explosion remains unclear, though the incident has raised questions about safety protocols at the oil storage facility.
events.micro_summary: Three workers died in an explosion at an Oil India facility in Assam's Dibrugarh district.
events.summary: Three workers died and several others were injured in an explosion and fire at Oil India Limited's Intermediate Tank Farm in Assam's Dibrugarh district during maintenance work on Friday.

events.extended_summary: A blast occurred at the Vasundhara Police Outpost in Ghaziabad on Friday night around 9 pm, damaging the facility by shattering two glass panes and cracking a wall. At the time, a Sub-Inspector and a delivery executive were present; the delivery executive sustained a head injury from shattered glass and was taken to a hospital, where he is now completely healthy, while police personnel remained unharmed. A banned group, Tehreek-ul Mujahideen Hindustan, claimed responsibility for the explosion, though police found no traces of gunpowder or explosives at the site. The area was cordoned off, and teams from the Forensic Science Laboratory, Bomb Disposal Squad, and Anti-Terrorism Squad collected evidence, with forensic samples sent to Agra for examination. Authorities are investigating all angles, including accidental explosion or deliberate conspiracy.
events.micro_summary: One person was injured in a blast at Ghaziabad's Vasundhara Police Outpost Friday night that damaged the facility.
events.summary: A blast at the Vasundhara Police Outpost in Ghaziabad on Friday night around 9 pm damaged the facility, shattering glass panes and cracking a wall, while injuring a delivery executive who was treated and recovered; police are investigating the cause.
